Coconut Kelz [5594

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Production

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
Being a “coconut” in South Africa is an offensive term describing someone who is black on the outside and white inside.

It is the name that satirist Lesego Thabli has adopted as her alter ego – Coconut Kelz.

When American author Rachel Dolezal, who was born to white parents, but identifies as black, was outed by the media. Coconut Kelz says she knew she had the same thing, but in reverse.

Her comedy started in 2016, when she made a video for her friends on twitter about the afro hair style debacle at Pretoria Girls High.

Lesego's rise to fame can be accredited to social media, where she launched a furious feat of selfie-style videos.
Unlike many social media stars, the satirical star is paving the way for tongue-in-cheek humour aimed at the state of politics in the country.

‘Kelz was kind of born in high school without realising it. I was at majority-white schools my whole life and was always very aware of the microaggressions the white girls displayed towards black girls (even unintentionally). I always thought it was quite bizarre that only the black girls seemed concerned with the difficult conversations around race, and that they appeared to be the only ones who seemed to have been taught since birth about white privilege.

‘I wanted to sort of play these sentiments back to them [white girls] in a funny way so they’d actually listen and not get defensive. I didn’t think it would grow like this.’

Following her comedic debut, The Coconut Show at Melville Comedy Club, Tlhabi is now making waves on the small screen with shorts on BET Africa aptly titled Coconut Kelz: The Election Special.

"I didn't do the character for any kind of career in the comedy scene; I just did it for my Facebook friends. So, it's awesome to see how it's grown and is my main career now, which I never expected," said Tlhabi.

Tlhabi said that the uniqueness and relatable banter of Coconut Kelz has played a part in her meteoric rise since conception two years ago on Facebook.
Tlhabi's character in contrast with their opinions on the elections and politics in the country.

Tlhabi has also been criticised for her satire which she has been labelled as a mockery of the lives of black people.
While the confusion with her satire has caused many to make incorrect assumptions about her intentions, Tlhabi has noticed more viewers are taking the time to explain her style of comedy.
Tlhabi also said that the likes of Evita Bezuidenhout have helped bring satire into the mainstream.
"Kelz is going to be everywhere, so everyone who hates her needs to turn off their TVs because I am going to be everywhere," said Tlhabi.

She recently published her book “ How to Survive this Shithole”. Thanks Donald Trump.

Carte Blanche is going to catch up on the year that has been with Coconut Kelz and ask her about how to Survive the Festive Season.

Coconut Kelz Script


V/O
Run off her feet with Christmas shopping we met Coconut Kelz at Fairlawns Spa for a soothing massage.

Devi
We thought you would appreciate this.

Kelz
I come to spas every day.

V/O
When dreaming of a white Christmas most people think of soft falling snow and frosted fur trees. The comedic character Cocunut Kelz’ dreams are far more literal.

Devi
“What are you doing for Christmas?”

Kelz
“I am gonna go to Finland because it is the whitest place I can think of snow and people.”

Link
It’s called satire a technique employed by writers to expose or criticise the ills of society. Coconut Kelz is shaking up all things race in South Africa.”

Devi
“When did you realise you were actually a white person tapped in a black person’s body?”

Kelz
“Ah Devs, literally since I was born, I have always known it, even when I cry as a baby I didn’t cry loud like an african child, I cried softly and more quite like a european child.

V/O
Coconut Kelz is a character dreamed up by comedien Lesego Tlhabi,


Kelz
“South Africa’s corruption is just dismal and like, it wasn’t even like this in apartheid, imagine that, apartheid was bad but Nkandla?”

Devi
“Lesego how did this all start?”

Lesego
“It was the Pretoria Girls High incident, many girls had afros at the school and were told that they were not allowed to have them. So I am one of those people who used to be a keyboard warrior, I would always have a very long status about political things happening in our country. “

Coconut
“So like I don’t know why you can’t wear your afro on the week and then have your normal straight hair on the week.

V/O
She started posting videos that created quite a stir.

Lesego
“My first reaction was hey it’s a bit controversial, people who know me will get it but I can’t deal with the opinions of everybody when they don’t know.”

Kelz
Howzit guys I am going to give you a weather forecast here, blue skies, beautiful day and not a single K in sight…what!”

Lesego
“I do go a lot to the extreme but for me the things that bothered me the most are not the racism that is the K word for me its lso using the tool to show the micro agressions like following you around the shop, locking your car door when you approach, that I deal with more.”

Kelz
“Hi guys I am just chilling in my hote here in Cape Town. And look what has started happening on the beach, they are gatherine, Ok they are moving now, it’s a pack, I don’t know if they are slaughtering a sheep or if they are collecting sea water.”

V/O
She has written a book to mend the gaps between the groups, to laugh and to survive South Africa together.

“When they think rainbow nation and Tar Tar Mandela’s dream “

Devi
“Sorry Who ?

Tar Tar?”

Kelz
“When he made that I have a dream speech he was talking about me, this is the dream for the future. White black in harmony.”



Coconut New Year

Kelz
“Some people said that black people don’t go on holiday they just go home. And I just didn’t identify with that statement so that’s when I realised that I have to get out of this place and just start going to Mauritius and living my best true life.”

V/O
It’s 2020, but for one South African Coconut Kelz, the year can’t start properly as her domestic staff have not returned from holiday.

Kelz
‘Boy, girl where are you? Come back. When do gardeners come back in December?”

“Feel so silly, I really miss girl and boy, it’s only been two hours since I have been back but I feel , I need their help.”

Link
Speaking to Coconut Kelz is like an out of body experience, she freely shares cringworthy thoughts and insists she is a white girl trapped in the body of a black woman.

V/O
Comedian Lesego Tlhabi created Coconut Kelz to parody some of the racial stereotyping that still takes place in South Africa, 25 years into our democracy.

Devi
“But Coconut Kelz is not an anomaly, she is not the only one? There plenty out there.”

Kelz
“Yes there really are and that is why I think the populariuty is rising because people, even white people, now realise how problematic my mom is or how racist my dad is. A lot of people who hate being called Coconut and it being a very aggressive bullying tactic, are kind of like thanks for making it lighter and for letting us laugh at ourselves and not feel such pain at the word.


V/O
There are no sacred cows, she has posted hosts of social media videos where she makes fun of issues in our country, like the water crisis in Cape Town.

Coconut
“I know people on twitter are like, I know finally white people will know what black people have been dealing with forever um like fetching water and bathing in a bucket, but like guys you cant start get used to something that you are not used to.”

Devi
“What point would you like to make?”

Kelz
“Its very easy for people to start getting wrapped up in the anger of it all, and now to see the shared ridiculousness because even if we are different, racially and I know I sound like Miss South Africa now, even though we have differences in race and class and thinsg like that we have shared frustrateions with current government wioth the opposition, I am trying to mend the gaps between the different groups and be able to laugh at the same thing together.”

V/O
In the new year Kelz is reaching out to try and build bridges with other race groups – like mine.

Kelz
“When you got your job on Carte Blanche , there goes the neighbourhood,

Devi
“Did you really think that”

Kelz
“I thought it would be downhill.”

Devi
“Down hill”

Kelz
“Oriental plaza just crazy”

Devi
“Show would go to the dogs. Do you still think that now?”

Kels
No, I don’t you speak very well,

Devi
For an indian

Kels
And that’s why I trusted you to interview me, before I was please bring Derek, but ja, you are doing well, you are doing so well.

Devi
Thank you.





Promo 1
She’s caused a media storm.
Coconut Kelz is a white woman trapped in a black woman’s body.

“I don’t know if they are slaughtering a sheep or if they collecting sea water.

Promo 2
Coconut Kelz is a character dreamed up by comedien Lesego Tlhabi, who uses her razor wit to cut straight to the heart of our country’s racial prejudice.

Promo 3
Even though we are 25 years into our democracy, race is still an issue. Coconut Kelz is out to heal the wounds with humour.
“Apartheid was bad but Nkandla?”
